verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'really dry itchy skin' 'all over my arms, um, and my hands mainly' and later adds 'my skin's quite red' and that it 'started a few days ago.'

Patient says 'I went swimming a few days ago.' and confirms symptoms started after that: Doctor: 'And did your symptoms start after you went swimming?' Patient: 'Uh, yes.' Also, coconut butter was ineffective: Doctor: 'so the coconut butter hasn't helped, with the itch?' Patient: 'No.'

Patient states 'I don't have any spots, and no fever, and I'm not sweating either.' Later denies vomiting, loose stools, and urinary problems: Doctor: 'no problems with vomiting, or loose stools?' Patient: 'No.' 'And your waterworks ... ?' Patient: 'Yep.' Appetite okay: Doctor: 'Your appetite's fine is it?' (no objection and patient says eating and drinking as normal).
When asked if she feels run-down or tired, patient replies: 'Uh, yeah, I think I have been, quite tired.'
Doctor asks about past skin problems: 'there's no, problems of skin problems in the past, things like eczema or, um, dermatitis?' Patient answers: 'Uh, no.'
Patient states she is currently taking a medication; doctor clarifies: 'Microgynon.' Patient: 'Yeah.' Doctor explains it's 'a contraceptive pill.'
When asked about allergies, patient says: 'I think, um, I might be lactose intolerant.'
Patient states: 'my dad has asthma, and, my mum has hayfever.'
After family history of asthma and hayfever, doctor asks: 'but any, again, any skin problems that you're aware of?' Patient: 'Uh, no.'
Patient says, 'I work as a teacher' and later confirmed as 'primary school teacher.' She notes, 'I've been really stressed at work for the past few days' and 'I've been working really long hours.'

Social history: Patient: 'Ohh, it's just me.' Doctor: 'Live alone?' Patient: 'Yep.' She denies smoking, alcohol, and drugs: 'no, I don't smoke.' 'Do you drink much in the way of alcohol?' Patient: 'Uh, no.' 'Recreational drugs?' Patient: 'No.'

Doctor summarizes: 'you've got a dry itchy rash on your, mainly your hands ... and your arms which started, perhaps after swimming a few days ago ... no other symptoms, you're feeling otherwise, well, no fevers, no bleeding or discharge from skin.' Doctor then says, 'I wonder whether you may have something called dermatitis.' This supports likely irritant/contact dermatitis of pruritic, erythematous, dry hands/arms without systemic symptoms.

Work stress and fatigue are explicitly linked: patient reports work has been 'really stressful' and that she has been 'quite tired.' Doctor notes 'sometimes stress can be a contributing factor' and asks if it might correlate to symptoms; patient answers, 'I certainly think so.'

Doctor: 'something called emollients, which can help with the dry, dry skin. And that's something you just need to kind of paste on, uh, on to your skin, uh, throughout the day for the next few days.' This corresponds to liberal, frequent application.
Doctor: 'we have steroid creams I can give you, um, which will help with the inflammation.' A short therapeutic course is the implied plan.

Doctor: 'you can also try antihistamines, so you can get things over the counter, Piriton, Loratadine, they can sometimes help with the itchiness.' This is use of oral antihistamines as needed for itch.

The doctor asks about potential triggers like 'shower gels, soaps, fabric cleaners' and notes swimming but does not advise avoiding pool chlorine, harsh soaps/detergents, or using barrier creams. These recommendations are not stated in the transcript.

Doctor: 'if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week, and we can have another look again, at your symptoms.' This is a return in about 1 week if no improvement; no explicit mention of 'sooner if worsen,' but the 1-week follow-up part is supported.
Although stress is discussed, there is no explicit advice in the transcript about rest, hydration, or good sleep hygiene.
The doctor acknowledges stress as a contributing factor but does not instruct the patient to monitor stress or suggest further support if it persists.
Doctor: 'I can give you a patient information leaflet about that, which gives a bit more information about the disease,' referring to dermatitis.

Doctor instructs: 'if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week.' This supports return in about 1 week if no improvement, though 'or sooner if symptoms worsen' is not explicitly stated.
